newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, awaits follow-through.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, awaits follow-through.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply higher, with the market at its strongest since just before the Sumitomo scandal broke in June 1996, but brokers were divided over how much higher the market could go.
"It may go a little bit higher but we will have to see some Chinese demand or unexpected supply disruptions to continue with this type of trend," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said.

The market should wait to see how much follow through there is on Thursday, and there was good resistance from 118 to 120 cents per pound, Rinehimer added. Some of copper's gains Wednesday came from a stronger LME base metals complex, with nickel gaining $200 a tonne in one day.
But other brokers said the copper price was still too low compared with the level of red metal stocks. "There is plenty of work left on the upside," one LME ring dealing member broker noted.

March COMEX, which now becomes the spot month due to February's expiry Wednesday, settled 3.40 cents firmer at 114.85 cents per pound, traded 114.90 to 111.40 cents. Most-active May also went out 3.40 cents up at 112.65 cents.
Copper was also helped by a strengthening backwardation on LME, up some $10 to $70/$73 since Tuesday.
Volume was estimated at a heavy 20,000 lots compared to Tuesday's 18,999 lots. Switches were estimated at 3,596 as the rollover from March to May was being completed.
